answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers (RLN) let a registered agent act once per epoch while staying anonymous. Its secret s is the intercept of a line whose slope is hash(s, epoch); each message carries a zk proof plus one point on that line. One point reveals nothing, but a second message that epoch hands anyone two points, which solve for s and unlock its deposit. A farm can't stretch one key into an ocean of posts or wake a tundra of idle keys for free, and the network never needs an atlas linking messages to members.
